status: Every coefficient is the author's assumption for an entertainment simulation. Sources support the historical context, not these probabilities.
step: one year of life; lives run until death or age 100
units: Money is counted in units, not dollars. 20 units = basic costs of one ordinary year. Savings are not capped.
gold: Miners only, years 1849-1855: yearly strike chance = strike_chance * 0.93^(year - 1849); gain uniform(strike_low, strike_high). After 1855 there are no strikes and the miner's base income is uniform(19, 35) before health and skill multipliers.
background_mortality: 1.5 * (0.0008 + 0.012 * exp((age - 58) / 10)) per year, drawn from a random stream shared by the three lives of the same world
extra_risk: If risk >= 55 and savings < 25, he takes extra risk with probability risk/150: income x1.25, wear x1.5, injury chance x1.6
giving_up: A miner switches to wage work after 2 poor years in a row (3 if risk >= 65) or when health < 32 without a lighter role; a merchant closes after 2 poor years in a row
emergency_aid: Up to 10 units from friends when support >= 55, at most once every 3 years
worlds: Paired design: world number N is the same world for all three jobs (shared epidemics, encounters, economy and mortality draws).

sources.supports: 1848-1855 context: mining, trade and supplying the miners
Discovery of gold in 1848 and the 1849 migration; the journey itself is not modeled
